tasks.title: Workspace, toolchain pin, and nine crate skeletons

details.goal: A building Cargo workspace at rust/ containing the nine crates of docs/my-product/RUST-MIGRATION.md §4, a pinned toolchain, and the dependency DAG declared so the boundary gate has something to check.
details.contract:
Workspace: nine members — core, store, domain, tools, index, telemetry, daemon, cli, boundary. Edition 2024, resolver 3, `rust-version = "1.100.0"`, one `[workspace.package] version = "0.6.0-beta.1"`, `Cargo.lock` committed. If a pinned version is not published at execution time, take the nearest published patch of the same minor and record the substitution in the task report — never a different major.
Dependency edges, exactly these and nothing else yet (declare only what the crate actually uses; the boundary test fails on an edge that is not listed):

- sangkar-store: sangkar-core, rusqlite = { version = "0.43", features = ["bundled"] }

- sangkar-tools: sangkar-core, sangkar-store, sangkar-domain

No cycle is possible by construction: `daemon` never depends on `cli`, and `cli` is the only crate that names `tools`, `index` and `daemon` together.
Module stubs each crate's `src/lib.rs` must declare (one empty file each, filled by later tasks):
- core: envelope, budget, cursor, errors, log, paths, instructions, config, global_config, repo_config, registry, pidlock, runtime
- store: schema, migrations, migrate, db, publish, lock, pool, and `read/{mod,nodes,edges,metrics,coverage,files,reader,context}.rs`

- tools: `mod.rs` + one module per tool (status, summary, trace, search, impact, expand, index), each with `manifest.rs` and `handler.rs`

- telemetry: record, telemetry, sink, identity, report, html, html_multi, serve, for_repo
- daemon: types, lifecycle, reconcile, main, cli
- cli: `main.rs` + args, render, repo, index_gate, mcp, dispatch, store_lifecycle
Do not add behaviour to any stub: every function body is `unimplemented!()` or absent. Do not create `rust/spikes/` (its own tasks do). Do not touch anything outside `rust/`.

Write `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` (channel 1.100.0, components rustfmt, clippy, profile minimal) and the workspace `Cargo.toml` with the nine members.
Write each crate's `Cargo.toml` with exactly the declared edges.
Write each crate's `src/lib.rs` module declarations and one empty file per module; `sangkar-cli/src/main.rs` with `fn main() {}`.
Write `rust/.gitignore` with `/target` and run `cargo fmt`.

tasks.title: core: error codes, stderr log, path helpers

details.goal: The three kernel primitives every other crate imports: the closed error-code union, the single stderr JSON-line logger, and the path/qualified-name helpers.
details.contract:
Port `src/shared/errors.ts` (81 lines) exactly:
```rust
pub const APP_ERROR_CODES: [&str; 12] = [
  "wrong_project_db", "unsupported_filesystem", "schema_too_new", "cursor_invalid",
  "cursor_expired", "cursor_mismatch", "budget_too_large", "bootstrapping", "not_found",
  "ambiguous", "index_locked", "internal"];
pub struct AppError { pub code: &'static str, pub message: String, pub hint: Option<String>,
                     pub retryable: bool, pub retry_after_ms: Option<u64> }
pub struct ErrorPayload { pub code: &'static str, pub message: String, pub hint: Option<String>,
                          pub retryable: Option<bool>, pub retry_after_ms: Option<u64> }
pub fn to_error_payload(e: &AppError) -> ErrorPayload;
```
Only the twelve codes are constructible; a misspelt code is a compile error, not a runtime `"internal"` coercion.
Port `src/shared/log.rs`: `pub fn log(level: Level, msg: &str, fields: &[(&str, serde_json::Value)])` writing ONE line of compact JSON `{ts,level,msg,...fields}` plus `\n` to stderr, `ts` in the same ISO-8601-with-milliseconds form the TypeScript side emits. Nothing else in the workspace may write to stderr outside this module, and nothing may write to stdout outside the CLI's renderer.
Port `src/shared/paths.ts` (93 lines): `normalize_rel`, `qn(rel, scope, name) -> "rel::Scope.name"`, `resolve_from(importer, specifier) -> Option<String>`, `prefix_bounds(prefix) -> {exact, low, high}` (half-open; `high` = exact + "0"), `is_under_prefix(path, prefix)`.
Unit tests must cover: the twelve codes and their serde spelling; `prefix_bounds` excluding the `src-old` sibling; `qn` for a dotted scope; `resolve_from` for `./`, `../`, bare and `node:`-style specifiers.
steps: Port errors.rs with the twelve codes as a `&'static str` newtype and a constructor that rejects an unknown code at compile time.
Port log.rs: one `serde_json::Map` in insertion order, written with a single `write_all` to stderr, flushed once.
Port paths.rs verbatim, including the `high = exact + "0"` trick and the `.`/`..` normalisation.
Write `tests/kernel.rs` covering the four cases above, including the `src-old` sibling.

`cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0.

One deliberate deviation from the sketch: AppError.code and ErrorPayload.code are `ErrorCode`, not bare `&'static str`, because a bare string cannot reject a misspelt code at compile time; as_str(), From<ErrorCode> for &'static str and PartialEq<&str> keep call sites plain (code == "not_found" works). tasks.title: core: envelope contract and the single truncation point

details.goal: The response contract and `emit()` — the only truncation point and the only minter of `next` — so no later task can invent a second way to answer.
details.contract:
Port `src/shared/envelope.ts` (270 lines). Exact wire shape:
```rust
pub struct Envelope<T> { pub status: Status, pub summary: String, pub read_status: ReadStatus,
  pub coverage: Coverage, pub totals: Totals, pub truncated: bool,
  pub truncation_reason: Option<TruncationReason>, pub next: Option<String>,
  pub next_tools: Vec<String>, pub payload: Option<T>, pub error: Option<ErrorPayload> }
pub enum Status { Ok, Ambiguous, NotFound, Error, Bootstrapping }      // serde: "ok"|"ambiguous"|"not_found"|"error"|"bootstrapping"
pub enum TruncationReason { Budget, ItemCap, Depth, Page }            // "budget"|"item_cap"|"depth"|"page"
pub enum TotalRelation { Eq, Gte }                                    // "eq"|"gte"
```
Metadata keys are ALWAYS present in this order: status, summary, read_status, coverage, totals, truncated, truncation_reason, next, next_tools, payload; `error` only when status is Error or Bootstrapping. `read_status` = {generation, indexed_at, stale, stale_reason?, stale_checked_at?, decisive?}; `coverage` = {complete, indexed, skipped, failed, unresolved_edges, not_indexed:[{path,reason}], tests?:{nodes,languages:[{language,nodes}]}}; `totals` = {total_relation} plus every `<list>_total` (number|null) plus optional `unresolved_material`, `candidates_shown`.
`relation_for(read_status, coverage) == Eq` iff `coverage.complete && coverage.unresolved_edges == 0 && !read_status.stale`, else Gte.
Constructors: `ok`, `ambiguous`, `not_found`, `fail`, `bootstrapping`, `with_payload`, `with_totals` — payload construction only through these, so a caller cannot omit `read_status` or `coverage`.
Port `src/shared/budget.ts` (415 lines): `BYTES_PER_TOKEN = 4`, `MAX_BUDGET_TOKENS = 32000`, `NEXT_TOKEN_RESERVE_CHARS = 384`, `EMPTY_LIST_BYTES = 2`, `MAX_TRIM_PASSES = 8`, `MAX_PIN_DEPTH = 6`; `emit(env, budget_tokens, mint: impl Fn(usize) -> String) -> Envelope<T>` with byte counting over compact JSON (`serde_json::to_vec`), largest-array-first tail dropping, pinned-path trimming of `coverage.not_indexed`, the eight-pass cap, the `dropped == 0 || still over` early return of the ORIGINAL envelope, the forced `truncated/truncation_reason/next/eq->gte` shape while planning, and `budgetFloorOf(value) = ceil(bytes/4)`. `budgetByteAllowance` refuses > 32000 with code `budget_too_large`.
The object-key order of `totals` and any payload is insertion order (serde_json `preserve_order` feature) because cursor tests and TOON tables depend on it.
Tests: every one of `tests/budget.test.ts`'s cases (empty envelope untouched, largest array cut first, no false `truncated`, no dead cursor, the 384-char reserve, `eq` downgraded only on a real cut), plus a golden byte-count for a fixed envelope.
steps: Add `serde_json = { features = ["preserve_order"] }` to sangkar-core and port envelope.rs types with `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` and explicit `skip_serializing_if` where a field is optional.
Implement the five constructors and `relation_for`.
Port budget.rs: byte count, list collection with pin depth, `plan_tail_drop`, `trim_coverage_tail`, the pass loop, and `emit`.
Write `tests/envelope_budget.rs` transcribing every assertion of `tests/budget.test.ts`.

`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-core --test envelope_budget` exits 0.
Done when: `grep -rn 'fn emit' rust/crates` shows exactly one definition, and the test file contains an assertion that an envelope over budget with a zero-length drop returns the input unchanged (`truncated == false`, `next == None`).

progress.detail: Ported src/shared/{envelope,budget}.ts into rust/crates/sangkar-core/src/{envelope,budget}.rs (526 + 465 lines) with 25 tests in tests/envelope_budget.rs (24 pass, 1 ignored). Trimmed surface: envelope.rs holds Status/TruncationReason/TotalRelation (#[serde(rename_all="snake_case")] + ALL + as_str), ReadStatus{generation,indexed_at,stale,stale_reason?,stale_checked_at?,decisive?}, Coverage{complete,indexed,skipped,failed,unresolved_edges,not_indexed,tests?}, TestCensus/TestCensusEntry/NotIndexedEntry, Totals as a PRIVATE serde_json::Map (preserve_order) whose builders always write total_relation first — Totals::new(relation).with_total("calls", Some(40)).with_total("gaps", None).with_unresolved_material(n).with_candidates_shown(n), plus get/as_map/relation/set_relation/with_relation — Envelope<T> declared in wire order with payload:Option<T> always present as null and error skip_serializing_if, EnvelopeSpec::new(summary, read_status, coverage) + with_totals/with_next_tools/with_truncation(reason,next), ok/ambiguous/not_found/fail/bootstrapping (BootstrappingSpec is nested because Rust has no struct inheritance; DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_MESSAGE) + with_payload/with_totals + relation_for. budget.rs: BYTES_PER_TOKEN=4, MAX_BUDGET_TOKENS=32_000, NEXT_TOKEN_RESERVE_CHARS=384 (private, like the TS), EMPTY_LIST_BYTES=2, MAX_TRIM_PASSES=8, MAX_PIN_DEPTH=6, budget_byte_allowance (refuses >32000 with budget_too_large + hint), budget_floor_of. Measurement is ONE compact serde_json::Value serialisation of the whole envelope, so what is measured and what is returned cannot drift; arrays are addressed by path (Step::Key/Index) instead of by reference, so the parent-detach rule is just a resolve() miss. trim_once ranks collection-time list bytes (ties to the longer list, as byLargestFirst does), plans the tail drop from per-item sizes (saved = size+1, capped at list_bytes-2), applies it to the draft's own copy, then hands the leftover to trim_coverage_tail (unpinned pass, then pinned; cut-once mask; drain+rebuild). Pass loop shape: `for _ in 0..8 { if measured <= budget { break } plan = trim_once(measured-budget); if plan.count == 0 { break } dropped += count; measured = json_len(draft) }`, then the two early returns of the ORIGINAL envelope (dropped == 0; measured still over the budget), then from_value + next = mint(dropped). A caller-flagged truncation is returned through `unless_flagged`, a nested fn INSIDE emit, so the eq->gte downgrade and the truncated/reason/next writes exist nowhere else: `grep -rn 'fn emit' rust/crates` = exactly one definition. Deviations: (1) emit returns Result<Envelope<T>, AppError> instead of Envelope<T>, because the sketch's budget_byte_allowance refusal cannot be expressed without a panic, which would abort a server on one bad budget; the only errors are budget_too_large and internal-for-unserialisable (unreachable for contract types); (2) emit needs T: Serialize + DeserializeOwned, since the draft is trimmed as a Value and parsed back — the Rust equivalent of the TS jsonClone/JSON.parse round trip — so handler payload types derive Deserialize alongside Serialize. Coverage of tests/budget.test.ts: 18 of 19 cases transcribed verbatim (including the 200-random-payload property with a ported mulberry32, the 32000 ceiling, the coverage trim, pin-vs-blind, detached-child counting, the floor-upwards sweep, and the below-the-floor case that also asserts a caller-flagged truncation survives); the 384-char reserve case uses a synthetic exactly-384-char token instead of createCursors (same byte-exact `bytes(out) <= budget*4` assertion and next == the caller's token, which is what fails if the reserve is lowered); the 19th (a cursor bound to a second repository cannot resume this page) is `#[ignore = "requires src/shared/cursor.ts (TASK-005)..."]` with its body printing the reason, because emit only calls mint and cursor.rs is not landed. Two TS assertions are inexpressible and were rewritten with comments rather than deleted: `expect(out).toBe(env)` (a Rust envelope is moved, so deep equality is the observable form) and `out.coverage.not_indexed !== env.coverage.not_indexed` (ownership); the "total_relation is not in the contract" assertion is now type-enforced. Golden byte count: the fixed envelope (fresh g-7f3a91 / 2026-11-17T13:50:15Z, clean coverage indexed 530, totals eq + calls_total 2, payload {base:"HEAD", calls:[2 app items]}) is 557 bytes and budget_floor_of == 140; that number was NOT self-derived — the same fixture run through Bun's JSON.stringify(ok(...)) under src/shared/envelope.ts produced the identical 557-byte string, character for character, which also confirms the totals/key order. Differential evidence beyond the unit tests: a temporary probe pushed the same 19 fixture/budget combinations through both implementations (coverage trim 700/800/900/1000/1200/2000, pin vs blind, 60 calls + 3 callees at 1000/700/500/400/300, nested groups + spill at 500/800/1200) and the emitted byte counts, truncated flags, reasons, relations, minted positions, next tokens and surviving list/path lengths were identical line for line after the tiebreak was added; the probe was then removed, as was the golden-string probe. TASK-027..TASK-033 must: build the payload with ok/ambiguous/not_found (or fail/bootstrapping for the error paths), build totals with Totals::new(relation).with_total("calls", Some(n)) — the list name WITHOUT the _total suffix, relation first, insertion order preserved — then `let emitted = emit(env, budget, |position| cursor.sign(...))?;` and refuse with budget_too_large when `budget_floor_of(&emitted) > budget`; mint is FnMut (so a closing mut Vec works), is called at most once and only on a real cut, and its token is not verified or measured beyond the 384-char reserve. clippy --all-targets is clean for both src files and the test; rustfmt --check clean on all three; the crate's other test targets (kernel 13 pass + 1 ignored, config_registry 69, cursor_interop 13) are unaffected.

details.goal: Opening a database must apply exactly the PRAGMAs the TypeScript side applies and refuse the filesystems it refuses; reads must reuse prepared statements through a bounded cache; one process must hold the write lock.
details.contract:
Port `src/shared/store/db.ts` (305 lines) and `src/shared/store/lock.ts` (228 lines).
Reader handle, in this order: `foreign_keys=ON`, `busy_timeout=10000`, `cache_size=-16384`, `mmap_size=268435456`, opened read-only (`OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY`, never a `file:` URI). Writer handle: `journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=NORMAL`, `cache_size=-65536`, `mmap_size=268435456`, `busy_timeout=10000`, `journal_size_limit=67108864`, `foreign_keys=ON`; after setting, assert `foreign_keys == 1`, `busy_timeout == 10000`, `cache_size == -65536`, `synchronous == 1`, `journal_size_limit == 67108864`; warn (not fail) when `mmap_size < 268435456`; a `journal_mode != "wal"` result is `AppError{code:"unsupported_filesystem"}`.
Prepared cache: own LRU keyed by a `&'static str` SQL key, `STATEMENT_CACHE_CAPACITY = 200` per handle, hit = delete+reinsert (move to MRU), miss = `prepare` then insert then evict the oldest key only, counters `hits/misses/evictions`, and `statement_cache_stats()` summing live caches (this feeds `status.payload.health.statement_cache_entries`). Never hold a statement across a transaction boundary.
`lock.rs`: `<dataDir>/write.lock` JSON `{"path":…, "pid":…, "startedAt":"<ISO>"}` created with `create_new(true)`; `STALE_AFTER_MS = 60_000`; `stale = pid.is_none() ? age > 60_000 : !is_alive(pid) || age > 60_000`; `is_alive` treats every errno except ESRCH as alive; reclaim = warn, unlink, retry, `ACQUIRE_ATTEMPTS = 3`; failure is `AppError{code:"index_locked", retryable:true, retry_after_ms:1000}`; `release` refuses to unlink a file whose pid is not ours; `heartbeat` touches mtime.
Tests: PRAGMA read-backs on a temp file; a WAL refusal simulated by an `:memory:` or `journal_mode=MEMORY` handle; cache hit/miss/eviction counters across 201 distinct keys; lock acquire, second acquire refusal, stale reclaim with a dead pid, release refusal.
steps: Port db.rs: `open_reader(path)`, `open_writer(path)`, pragma application with read-back assertions, and the LRU wrapper.
Add `Conn` holding the `Connection`, its cache and the path, with `prepared(sql_key, f)` matching the TypeScript call shape.
Port lock.rs with the JSON body, the liveness test and the three attempts.
Write tests/db_lock.rs over temp dirs.

`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-store --test db_lock` exits 0.

Writer applies journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, cache_size=-65536, mmap_size=268435456, busy_timeout=10000, journal_size_limit=67108864, foreign_keys=ON in that order, then asserts foreign_keys==1, busy_timeout==10000, cache_size==-65536, synchronous==1, journal_size_limit==67108864 by read-back; journal_mode!=wal returns AppError{unsupported_filesystem} with the hint "WAL needs a writable local directory; point --data-dir at one", which :memory: (journal_mode answers "memory") reaches. Conn owns the Connection, path, mode and an Arc<Mutex> LRU of &'static str keys capped at STATEMENT_CACHE_CAPACITY=200: a hit removes+re-pushes the key (MRU) with no eviction, a miss counts before build (so a failed prepare inserts nothing, as the TS does), inserts after the build and pop_fronts exactly one key; statements themselves live in rusqlite's per-connection cache, also capped at 200, because a Statement<'conn> cannot be stored beside the Connection that owns it without unsafe. Statement keys 0..200 (201 distinct) give size=200, misses=201, hits=0, evictions=1; re-using the first key misses again (misses=202, evictions=2) proving the oldest key was the one evicted, and a retained key then hits. statement_cache_stats() sums Weak<Mutex<StatementCache>> entries so a closed handle stops counting. lock.rs writes <dataDir>/write.lock as {"path":…,"pid":…,"startedAt":"<ISO>"} by hand (JSON.stringify key order and escaping) via create_new(true), STALE_AFTER_MS=60_000, stale = pid.is_none() ? age>60_000 : !is_alive(pid)||age>60_000, hand-scanned pid (positive integer only, torn body => None => age rule); is_alive is /proc/<pid> existence because sangkar-store may not gain libc and the migration ships Linux x64 (the plan's maintainer decision), and it keeps the errno rule: only a missing entry counts as dead, any other error stays alive. The remaining contract cases are separate named tests: reader pragmas plus write refusal (`a_reader_applies_its_own_pragmas_and_refuses_a_write`: foreign_keys=1, busy_timeout=10000, cache_size=-16384, mmap_size=268435456), `a_filesystem_that_cannot_hold_a_wal_is_unsupported` (`:memory:` -> unsupported_filesystem), `a_uri_filename_is_refused_before_sqlite_sees_it` (no `file:` URI ever reaches SQLite), `a_reader_refuses_a_missing_database_instead_of_creating_one`, and lock coverage for acquire / second-acquire `index_locked` / stale-by-dead-pid / stale-by-age-even-when-live / torn body / release-refusal-for-another-pid / heartbeat. `db.rs:304` calls `set_prepared_statement_cache_capacity(STATEMENT_CACHE_CAPACITY)`, so rusqlite's per-connection statement cache is capped at the same 200 as our LRU rather than its default. Accepted deviations: (1) actual `Statement` reuse rides rusqlite's connection cache while our LRU owns the keys, the policy and the counters that feed `status.payload.health.statement_cache_entries`, because a `Statement<'conn>` cannot be stored beside its own `Connection` without unsafe — the observable contract (bounded, LRU, counted) holds; (2) the in-memory pager answers `PRAGMA mmap_size` with no row, which is treated as `granted=0` and warns, so `:memory:` reaches the `unsupported_filesystem` verdict where the TypeScript would throw `internal` at the mmap read-back first — `:memory:` is not a real target, and both end in a refusal rather than a silent misconfiguration; (3) the ISO-8601-milliseconds formatter is duplicated in `lock.rs` because `sangkar-core`'s is private, and `is_alive` reads `/proc/<pid>` instead of `kill(pid,0)` because no `libc` dependency may be added — this is the Linux x64 target the maintainer decision scoped the first release to, and it is commented as such; (4) log fields use `.into()` because `sangkar-store` has no `serde_json`, and no dependency was added.

details.goal: Never publish a partial graph: a reader must keep serving the previous generation while a new one is written to a stage, sealed, and renamed over the live file.
details.contract:
Port `src/shared/store/publish.ts` (434 lines). Exact path and sequences:
- `STAGE_INFIX = ".stage."`; `stage_path(live) = format!("{live}.stage.{hex12}")` from 6 random bytes.
- `stage(live, seed_from_live: bool)`: when seeding, open the source read-only and run `VACUUM INTO ?`; otherwise create the file. Report `seeded_from: Live|Empty`.
- `begin_write(stage)` returns a scope whose `transaction(|tx| …)` runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and commits/rolls back; `close()` runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` then `PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE` and only then closes the handle (the ordering exists because a live statement defers `sqlite3_close` and leaves -wal/-shm, which makes the journal switch fail with SQLITE_BUSY — copy the comment, not just the code).
- `seal(stage)`: fresh handle -> `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` (`busy` must be 0) -> `journal_mode = DELETE` (must read back `delete`) -> `synchronous = FULL` (must read back 2) -> `quick_check(1)` (must be exactly `["ok"]`); any deviation is `AppError{code:"internal"}` with the observed value.
- `publish(stage, live)`: `rename()` then remove `<live>-wal`, `<live>-shm`, `<live>-journal` if present.
- `discard(stage)`: remove the stage plus its three sidecars, never the live file.
- `with_stage(live, f)` guarantees `discard` on every error path, including a panic (drop guard).
Tests: publish an empty stage over an existing database and assert the old content is gone and the new schema_version is present; a failing callback leaves the live file untouched and no `.stage.*` behind; seal detects a deliberately broken `journal_mode`; `quick_check` failure is reported with its text.
steps: Port the stage/seal/publish/discard primitives with the exact PRAGMA order and read-backs.
Implement the write scope with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and the close ordering.
Implement `with_stage` with a drop guard for the discard path.
Write tests/publish.rs over temp directories, asserting that no `.stage.` file survives any path.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-store --test publish` exits 0.
Done when: a test publishes over a populated database and shows the previous rows gone while the parent directory listing has zero `.stage.*` leftovers, and a test forcing a seal failure leaves the live file byte-identical (compare `sha256`).

progress.detail: Ported src/shared/store/publish.ts statement for statement into rust/crates/sangkar-store/src/publish.rs. SEAL: fresh read-write handle (no CREATE, so a missing stage is an error) -> PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) requiring exactly one row with busy==0 -> PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE read back and required to be exactly "delete" -> PRAGMA synchronous = FULL read back and required to be exactly 2 -> PRAGMA quick_check(1) required to be exactly the single row "ok". Every deviation is AppError{code:"internal"} carrying the observed value (e.g. "journal_mode is wal, expected delete, on <path>", "quick_check failed on <path>: <text>"/"synchronous is 1, expected 2"), with the TypeScript's hints. PUBLISH: refuse a path without STAGE_INFIX, refuse a missing stage, rename() stage over live FIRST, then remove <live>-wal/-shm/-journal (the rename order is preserved with its reason: deleting the old -wal before the swap would throw away committed data). DISCARD removes the stage plus its three sidecars and never the live file. WriteScope::close runs wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) then journal_mode = DELETE and only then drops the handle, with the copied reason: SQLite defers sqlite3_close while a statement is referenced, so a closed-but-lingering connection keeps -wal/-shm and the journal switch from another connection fails SQLITE_BUSY. stage_path = <live>.stage.<12 lowercase hex>; the 6 bytes come from RandomState::new() (stdlib, OS-seeded per instance) hashed with nanos + pid + a stack address and rendered with {byte:02x} - the same technique sangkar-core/config.rs uses for its cursor key, no rand/getrandom dependency added. with_stage returns stage -> callback -> seal -> publish with a StageGuard whose Drop calls discard_quietly, so an Err, a `?` and an unwind all discard; the panic path is tested with catch_unwind and a temporarily silenced panic hook. tasks.title: Spike: prove the MCP transport frames like the TypeScript SDK

details.goal: Decide whether rmcp 3.11.0's stdio transport can reproduce the TypeScript server's wire behaviour (newline-delimited JSON-RPC, no Content-Length headers, in-band error envelopes), which TASK-034 depends on.
details.contract:
`rust/spikes/mcp/` is a standalone package (empty `[workspace]` in its Cargo.toml) depending on rmcp = "3.11" and tokio; it serves ONE tool named `echo` whose handler returns `{content:[{type:"text",text:"<the args as JSON>"}], isError:false}` and declares `capabilities.tools`, an `instructions` string, and a tool input schema produced from a raw JSON object (not a zed/derive macro).
`scripts/parity/mcp-session.ts` runs under bun and records a session against the TypeScript server (`~/.bun/bin/bun run bin/sangkar.ts mcp --repo-root .`): `initialize` (protocolVersion, capabilities, clientInfo), the `notifications/initialized` notification, `tools/list`, one `tools/call` for `status` with `{}`, and one `tools/call` with a deliberately invalid argument. It writes `rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session.ndjson`: one line per frame, each `{"dir":"c2s"|"s2c","raw":"<the exact bytes without the trailing newline>"}`. It also writes `rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session_ts_only.json` holding the TypeScript server's responses for later comparison in TASK-034.
The spike must answer: (a) does the frame carry only `\n` terminators, (b) does the server require `notifications/initialized` before answering, (c) is an unknown tool or a bad argument answered in-band with `isError:true` rather than a JSON-RPC error, (d) does `tools/list` return the raw schema object unchanged.
Write `rust/spikes/mcp/DECISION.md`: verdict, the four answers with the observed bytes, and — if rmcp cannot do one of them — name the hand-rolled JSON-RPC fallback (~400 lines over tokio stdin/stdout lines).
steps: Create the standalone rmcp spike serving one `echo` tool with a raw JSON schema.
Write the bun recorder against the TypeScript server and commit the NDJSON plus the TS-only responses.
Replay the recorded client frames against the spike and diff what comes back.
Record the four answers with the observed bytes.
Write DECISION.md with the verdict and the fallback named.
details.verify:
`~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/mcp-session.ts` writes `rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session.ndjson` with at least 6 lines and exits 0.
A replay (`~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/mcp-session.ts --replay rust/spikes/mcp/target/debug/sangkar-spike-mcp`) completes the `initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call` sequence without a timeout.
Done when: DECISION.md answers (a)–(d) and `rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session.ndjson` is committed.

progress.detail:
Verdict: rmcp 3.11.0's stdio transport reproduces the TypeScript SDK's wire behaviour on all four counts, so the ~400-line hand-rolled JSON-RPC over tokio stdin/stdout lines (RUST-MIGRATION.md §8 R2's fallback) is NOT needed and should not be built. (a) Framing is newline-only on both: the TypeScript session is 4 s2c frames / 14766 bytes / 4 '
' / 0 CR bytes / 0 "Content-Length" / 0 bytes left after the last terminator (exit 0); the spike is 933 bytes / 4 '
' / 0 CR / 0 Content-Length / 0 leftover (exit 0); rmcp agrees in its own source — JsonRpcMessageCodec reads one line at a time at b'
' (transport/async_rw.rs:148) and appends buf.put_u8(b'
') (line 615). (b) Neither server gates on notifications/initialized: both answer tools/list sent straight after initialize (TS verified by hand on a pipe, spike recorded in rust/spikes/mcp/replay_s2c.ndjson as session "no-initialized"), and the notification itself produces no frame on either side. (c) Errors stay in-band: TS answers tools/call status {"budget":"many"} as a JSON-RPC *result* with isError:true ("status received an invalid "budget" argument"); the spike answers the replayed frame as {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"no tool named "status" in this surface; this spike registers: echo"}],"isError":true}} and a probe as {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":11,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"echo could not answer: `text` must be a string"}],"isError":true}} — CallToolResult::error, never Err(McpError) — while a good echo call returns isError:false with the arguments as JSON. (d) tools/list returns the declared schema unchanged in content but with every object's keys sorted (serde_json Map is a BTreeMap by default): declared {"$schema","type","properties":{"text","count"},"required","additionalProperties"} came back as {"$schema","additionalProperties","properties":{"count","text"},"required","type"}; rebuilding the spike with serde_json/features=["preserve_order"] put the declared order on the wire verbatim, so byte-level schema parity is one feature flag away. Three caveats for TASK-034, all measured: rmcp spawns each request handler (service.rs, Event::PeerMessage Request arm) so responses are not in request order — a burst of five came back as ids 1,5,3,2,4 (and 1,5,2,3,4) while the TS server answered 1,2,3,4,5, so compare by id and not by arrival; rmcp does not validate arguments against inputSchema, so the ported parseArgs must own that check and answer CallToolResult::error; and resultType appears only for peers negotiating 2026-07-28 (correctly absent for the recorded 2025-11-25 client). Evidence: rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session.ndjson holds 9 frames (5 c2s, 4 s2c, {"dir","raw"} per line, deterministic across reruns, at least 6 as required), rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session_ts_only.json holds the TS server's raw answers plus its framing counters, rust/spikes/mcp/replay_s2c.ndjson holds the spike's 22 frames, and rust/spikes/mcp/DECISION.md records the verdict, the four answers with the observed bytes, the preserve_order experiment and the named-but-unneeded fallback. Reproduce: `~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/mcp-session.ts` (exit 0) and `~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/mcp-session.ts --replay rust/spikes/mcp/target/debug/sangkar-spike-mcp` (exit 0, initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call all answered, no timeout); every TS invocation used --data-dir /tmp/sangkar-parity-mcp-session and .sangkar/graph.db was never opened (mtime unchanged). TASK-034 must register the seven tools through ServerHandler/list_tools + Tool::new with the manifests' raw JSON schemas, port answer() onto CallToolResult::success/error including the unknown-tool and bad-argument paths, compare against mcp_session_ts_only.json by request id as parsed JSON (enable serde_json/features=["preserve_order"] first if the bar is byte equality), and keep --data-dir in every parity test.

Orchestrator verification (independent runs): `~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/mcp-session.ts` exit 0, wrote `rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session.ndjson` with 9 frames (5 c2s + 4 s2c, contract floor was 6); decoded every frame and the sequence is exactly as contracted — initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list (s2c id=2 carries `tools`), tools/call status {} (s2c id=3 carries content+isError), tools/call status {"budget":"many"} (s2c id=4 carries content+isError, i.e. in-band, not a JSON-RPC error). Replay `~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/mcp-session.ts --replay rust/spikes/mcp/target/debug/sangkar-spike-mcp` exit 0 with ids 1-4 all answered, no timeout; the 53 MB spike binary is gitignored (`git status -uall | grep spikes/mcp/target` is empty, `rust/spikes/mcp/.gitignore` holds `/target`). DECISION.md answers (a)-(d) with measured bytes. VERDICT: rmcp 3.11.0 suffices on all four counts; the ~400-line hand-rolled JSON-RPC fallback that RUST-MIGRATION.md §8 R2 held in reserve is NOT needed. Three findings TASK-034 must honour: (1) rmcp dispatches concurrently, so arrival order is not 1,2,3,4 — a burst came back 1,5,3,2,4 and 1,5,2,3,4 on reruns, so the parity test must correlate by request id, never by arrival order; (2) `inputSchema` member ORDER is normalised by rmcp's serde_json without `preserve_order` — the members survive, the order does not, so TASK-034/025 must enable `preserve_order` in the CLI crate or accept sorted keys deliberately; (3) rmcp does not validate arguments against `inputSchema`, so argument refusal stays in the ported parseArgs answering CallToolResult::error. Deviation: the spike's `echo` carries a two-line argument check because (c) is unobservable on a tool that accepts anything; recording and replay are byte-identical across reruns, and `graph.db` mtime was unchanged because every TS invocation used a temp `--data-dir`.

tasks.title: Parity harness: three fixture repositories and the golden capture

details.goal: A checked-in oracle bank: three fixture repositories, a script that captures every tool's TypeScript envelope into rust/tests/golden/**, and a structural comparator that survives the deletion of TypeScript.
details.contract:
Fixtures (checked in, small, no `node_modules`):
- `polyglot/` — one small file per language of the 12 rows, plus a caller chain (a calls b calls c), a class with a subclass, a test file that calls a production function, a duplicate name in two files, and an import that cannot resolve. Must be big enough that `trace --depth 2`, `impact --paths`, and `expand what=members|edges|source|outline` all return non-empty answers.
- `broken/` — a file with a syntax error, one binary file (a 1 KB PNG header is enough), a directory made unreadable at test time (not in git), a 600 KB file, a file with a unicode path, and an empty file.
- `empty/` — a directory with only a `.gitignore`.
`scripts/parity/capture-goldens.ts` runs under bun. For each fixture it uses a TEMP data dir (`--data-dir <temp>`) so nothing is written inside the checked-in fixture, then for each of the 7 tools runs this fixed matrix with `--json --repo-root <fixture> --data-dir <temp>`:
- `status` — `{}` and `{paths:["src"]}`
- `summary` — `{scope:"repo"}` and `{scope:"area", target:"src"}` (the `change` scope is captured once with `base: "HEAD"`)
- `trace` — `{query:"<a function that exists in polyglot>", depth:2}` and `{query:"<the duplicate name>", depth:1}`
- `search` — `{query:"<a token present in polyglot>"}` and `{query:"<the token>", kind:"function", path:"src"}`
- `impact` — `{paths:["<a file that exists>"], depth:2}` and `{base:"HEAD"}`
- `expand` — `{target:"<a qn from the pending status answer>", what:"members"}` and `{what:"outline"}` for the same target
- `index` — `{mode:"fast"}` on a copy of the fixture (the only tool that writes)
Write `rust/tests/golden/<fixture>/<tool>.json` as `{args: [...], stdout: "<exact bytes>", exit_code: n}`. Also capture one paginated call per cursor-bearing tool (`trace`, `search`, `summary`, `impact`, `status`) with a small budget so the `next` token is a golden.
`scripts/parity/compare.py` is dependency-free python3: given two `{args, stdout, exit_code}` JSON files it compares STRUCTURALLY (same key sets at every depth, same primitive values, same array order and length, same exit code) and prints a JSON-pointer path for each difference, exiting 1 on any. A TOON stdout falls back to a byte comparison with a clear message that structural comparison needs `--json` goldens.
`.sangkarignore` gains the single line `rust/tests/parity/fixtures/` so this repository's own index does not absorb the fixtures' deliberate failures; `~/.bun/bin/bun test tests/discover.test.ts` must stay green.
`rust/tests/parity/README.md` (short) explains: how to recapture, why the cursor key is fixed, why fixtures use a temp data dir, and that the goldens are the only oracle after phase_5.

Write capture-goldens.ts with the argument matrix and the fixed cursor key.
Write compare.py with the structural comparison and the pointer diff.
Add the `.sangkarignore` line and confirm discovery still passes.
Write the README and commit the captured goldens.

tasks.title: The boundary gate: crate DAG, rusqlite location, stdout discipline

details.goal: The six module rules of .agents/prompts/rules.md must fail the build in Rust the way tests/boundary.test.ts fails it in TypeScript, so no later task can quietly add a forbidden import.
details.contract:
`sangkar-boundary` reads `rust/crates/*/Cargo.toml` as text (no metadata crate) and asserts the exact dependency table, both directions:
```
core     -> (none)
store    -> core
 domain   -> core, store
 tools    -> core, store, domain
 index    -> core, store, domain
 telemetry-> core
 daemon   -> core, store, index, telemetry
 cli      -> core, store, domain, tools, index, telemetry, daemon
 boundary -> (none)
```
A `sangkar-*` dependency not in that set is a failure naming the crate and the edge. Third-party edges are not checked except `rusqlite`, which must appear in `sangkar-store`'s manifest and nowhere else.
Three source scans, all under `rust/crates`:
1. stdout discipline: no `println!`, `print!`, `eprintln!` or `std::io::stdout` in `*/src/**/*.rs` (the logger writes to stderr through `std::io::stderr`); tests under `*/tests/**` are exempt.
2. tool isolation: no `crate::tools::` inside `sangkar-tools/src/tools/**` (a tool may not name another tool).
3. no `TODO(phase` markers: a phase hand-off comment is a plan violation, not a note.
The test must be self-proving: one `#[test]` writes a temporary crate manifest with a forbidden `core -> store` edge and asserts the checker rejects it, so a broken scanner cannot pass by finding nothing.
steps: Write a small manifest scanner (sections, path dependencies) with unit cases for `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]` and inline tables.
Encode the expected DAG table and the rusqlite rule.
Write the three source scans with the exemption rules.
Add the negative self-test using a temp directory.
Run it and confirm it fails after temporarily adding `sangkar-store` to core's manifest, then revert.

`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-boundary` exits 0.
The deliberate-edit check from step 5 fails with a message containing `sangkar-core -> sangkar-store`.
Done when: `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-boundary -- --nocapture` prints the scanned crate count (9) and the DAG check counts (8 edges checked).

progress.detail: Two files written, nothing else touched: rust/crates/sangkar-boundary/src/lib.rs (the gate, no dependencies, root derived from env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR)/../..) and tests/dag.rs (8 tests). Raw text parsing, no metadata crate and no dev-dependencies (boundary's Cargo.toml is byte-identical). Scanner: a small TOML reader (strip_comment, section_header including [[bin]], brace_depth for multi-line inline tables, inline_field for path = "…", split_top_level, dotted keys, [target.'cfg(..)'.dependencies] via last-segment match) feeding Dependency{name,table,path}; DAG as a 9-row public const; rusqlite required in sangkar-store's [dependencies] and rejected anywhere else (message names crate -> edge); a sangkar-* dep in ANY table not in the row fails, and a required edge missing from [dependencies] fails (both directions). Source scans walk crates/*/src and crates/*/tests only (never rust/target or rust/spikes) and match code, not prose: strip_comments_and_strings removes //, nested /* */, "…", r#/br# raw strings, char literals and keeps newlines, so sangkar-core/src/log.rs may write about eprintln! in a doc comment or a string and still pass; the macro check requires the identifier boundary plus a following ! (so eprintln! is not "println!"), and std::io::stdout is matched after whitespace compaction. Two layout adaptations: (1) the tool rule follows TASK-001's real src/<tool>/ layout — tool modules are discovered from src/* directories, so no crate::tools anywhere under sangkar-tools/src (the crate root is exempt, declaring the modules is its job) and no crate::<other tool> under src/<tool>/, braced groups (crate::{a, b}) included; intent identical to "a tool may not name another tool", shared machinery being in core/store/domain which the DAG already enforces. (2) the eprintln! ban holds for every file with no allowlist (the marker/matcher constants are assembled with concat! so this crate passes its own scan; the gate caught my own doc comment mentioning the marker during development and the comment was reworded, not excepted). Self-proof: a_forbidden_core_to_store_edge_is_rejected mirrors crates/*/Cargo.toml into a TempTree (Drop removes it), asserts the copy passes, injects sangkar-store into core's [dependencies] at the table header and asserts exactly one violation containing "sangkar-core -> sangkar-store" with no unrelated violation. Step 5 on the real tree: adding sangkar-store to sangkar-core makes cargo itself refuse first — "error: cyclic package dependency" (store -> core), so the gate never runs; reverted immediately. A non-cyclic forbidden edge on the real tree (sangkar-telemetry -> sangkar-domain) does reach the gate and fails with "sangkar-telemetry -> sangkar-domain: sangkar-* dependency is not in the DAG (declared in [dependencies]; allowed: sangkar-core)"; reverted. Both deliberate manifest edits were reverted: `git diff --stat rust/crates/sangkar-core/Cargo.toml rust/crates/sangkar-telemetry/Cargo.toml` is empty. (2) The `eprintln!` ban holds for every file including `log.rs` with no allowlist, implemented by stripping comments and string literals before matching — which is why `log.rs`'s doc comment mentioning stdout does not trip it.
